subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: What privacy and exposure boundary should OpenClaw use for inbound WhatsApp call events from Baileys?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but recording or exposing call metadata changes what agents and plugins can infer about user contacts, timing, and group activity.

options.title: Opt-in sanitized call activity
options.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp-plugin setting or hook that exposes only sanitized call activity after existing sender/account access-control checks, with retention and docs spelled out.

options.title: Defer to a generic channel-event API
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers define a broader channel event surface for calls, reactions, and other non-message activity.

options.title: Do not track calls
options.body: Reject inbound call tracking if call metadata is considered too sensitive for OpenClaw to retain or expose to agents.

recommendation.title: Opt-in sanitized call activity
recommendation.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp-plugin setting or hook that exposes only sanitized call activity after existing sender/account access-control checks, with retention and docs spelled out.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the adjacent WhatsApp call-tool work and already scoped this issue as WhatsApp-plugin-owned with privacy/access-control requirements.
